questions.text: The "Big Three" forms of business ownership (Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Corporation) are becoming the "Big Four". What is the fourth form?
questions.explanation: The Big Four are Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Corporation, and Limited Liability Company. Franchising is not a form of ownership; it is an operation option.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT listed as something the form of ownership affects?
questions.explanation: The form of ownership affects operation, start-up costs, profit distribution, taxes, and management succession plans. Product design is not on the list.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as ADVANTAGES of a sole proprietorship?
questions.explanation: The listed advantages are ease of formation, retention of control, pride of ownership, retention of profits, and possible tax advantages. A sole proprietor has unlimited liability, not limited.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as DISADVANTAGES of a sole proprietorship?
options: Limited ability to attract and maintain talented employees
questions.explanation: The disadvantages are limited financial resources, unlimited liability, limited ability to attract and maintain talented employees, and lack of permanence. Double taxation is a disadvantage of corporations.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as ADVANTAGES of a partnership?
questions.explanation: Partnership advantages are pooled financial resources, shared responsibilities, ease of formation, and tax advantages. Lack of continuity is listed as a disadvantage.

questions.text: Besides unlimited liability, disagreements, and difficulty in withdrawing from the agreement, a disadvantage of partnerships is lack of ___.
questions.explanation: The four partnership disadvantages are unlimited liability, disagreements, difficulty in withdrawing from the agreement, and lack of continuity.

questions.text: Match each type of partnership to its description.
allChoices: Includes at least one general partner and at least one limited partner
All partners are actively involved but have some form of limited liability
All partners may participate in management and share in profits and losses
Parents are general partners and children are limited partners

pairs.match: Includes at least one general partner and at least one limited partner
All partners are actively involved but have some form of limited liability
All partners may participate in management and share in profits and losses
Parents are general partners and children are limited partners

questions.explanation: A limited partnership has at least one general and one limited partner. In a limited liability partnership all partners are active but have some limited liability (the amount differs per state). In a general partnership all partners can manage and share profits and losses. A family limited partnership has parents as general partners and children as limited partners.

questions.text: In a limited partnership, what is the limitation on the limited partner(s)?
options: They cannot share in the profits
They cannot actively participate in management
questions.explanation: All partners contribute financially and share in the profits, but limited partners cannot actively participate in management, and their liability is limited.

questions.text: Which of the following are strategies or effects of a Family Limited Partnership?
options: Protects family assets from creditors and lawsuits
Guarantees that it will never be audited by the IRS
Parents transfer assets to the limited partners while still maintaining control
questions.explanation: Parents keep control while transferring assets, which reduces gift and inheritance taxes and protects assets from creditors and lawsuits. The module also warns that family limited partnerships can attract tax auditors.

questions.text: A corporation is a legal entity, separate and distinct from its owners.
questions.explanation: The module describes a corporation as "a legal entity, separate and distinct from its owners."

questions.text: Who elects the Board of Directors, which establishes the corporation's mission and objectives?
questions.explanation: Corporations are owned by stockholders, and the Board is elected by the stockholders to represent their interests.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as ADVANTAGES of a corporation?
questions.explanation: The advantages are limited liability, permanence, easy transfer of ownership, ability to raise capital, and specialized management. Double taxation is a disadvantage.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as DISADVANTAGES of a corporation?
questions.explanation: The disadvantages are expense and complexity of formation and operation, double taxation, paperwork and regulation, and conflicts of interest. Easy transfer of ownership is an advantage.

questions.text: Match each type of corporation to one of its characteristics.
allChoices: No more than 100 stockholders
Owners can participate in management while maintaining limited liability
Can't distribute dividends

pairs.match: Owners can participate in management while maintaining limited liability

questions.explanation: An S corporation is limited to 100 stockholders, who must be US citizens or permanent residents. A statutory close corporation lets owners take part in management while keeping limited liability. A nonprofit corporation has no stockholders and can't distribute dividends or make political donations.

questions.text: Which of the following is a limitation of a nonprofit corporation?
options: Its earnings are taxed like any other corporation
Contributions made to it are not tax-deductible
questions.explanation: A nonprofit may have dues-paying members but no stockholders, can't distribute dividends or make political donations, and must keep accurate records to document its tax exemption. Its earnings are exempt from income taxes and contributions are tax-deductible.

questions.text: Which of the following is a limitation of an S Corporation?
options: Earnings are taxed separately by the IRS
It may have no more than 100 stockholders
It can't have a board of directors
questions.explanation: S corporations may have no more than 100 stockholders, who must be US citizens or permanent residents. Their key advantages are that the IRS does not tax earnings separately and stockholders have limited liability.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as ADVANTAGES of a Limited Liability Company (LLC)?
questions.explanation: LLC advantages are limited liability, tax pass-through, simplified management and operation, and flexible ownership. Franchise taxes are a disadvantage.

questions.text: Which of the following is a DISADVANTAGE of an LLC?
questions.explanation: The LLC disadvantages are franchise taxes, foreign status in other states, state law differences, and being limited to select industries.

questions.text: On the "Comparing Business Forms" spectrum, which form has the HIGHEST degree of personal liability and the LOWEST degree of complexity and perpetuity?
questions.explanation: Going from sole proprietorships to partnerships to corporations, personal liability goes from high to low while complexity and perpetuity go from low to high.

questions.text: In corporate restructuring, what is an acquisition?
options: Two companies agree to a combination of equals
A firm sells its brand name to a franchisee
A firm splits into two smaller companies
questions.explanation: An acquisition is when one firm buys another. A merger is when two companies agree to a combination of equals.

questions.text: Which of the following do corporations look for when restructuring through mergers and acquisitions?
questions.explanation: Corporations look for growth opportunities, operational efficiencies, and competitive advantages.

questions.text: Match each type of merger to its definition.
allChoices: Combines firms in the same industry
Combines companies with a buyer-seller relationship
Combines unrelated companies

pairs.match: Combines firms in the same industry
Combines companies with a buyer-seller relationship

questions.explanation: Horizontal mergers combine firms in the same industry (to increase size, market power and efficiency). Vertical mergers combine companies with a buyer-seller relationship (tighter integration and more control). Conglomerate mergers combine unrelated companies (to increase diversity).

questions.text: Match each example from the module to the type of merger it illustrates.
allChoices: Horizontal
Vertical
Conglomerate
questions.explanation: The module's examples are AT&T and SBC (horizontal), Time Warner and Turner Broadcasting (vertical), and GE acquiring RCA (conglomerate).

questions.text: Franchising is a form of business ownership, just like a sole proprietorship, partnership, or corporation.
questions.explanation: The module says franchising is "not a form of ownership but an operation option."

questions.text: In franchising, what does the franchisee use?
options: The brand name, trademark and practices of the franchisor
The tax exemption of the franchisor
questions.explanation: The franchisee uses the brand name, trademark and practices of the franchisor, for a price.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as ADVANTAGES of franchising?
questions.explanation: The advantages are less risk, training and support, brand recognition, and access to funding. Lack of control is a disadvantage.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT listed as a disadvantage of franchising?
questions.explanation: The disadvantages are costs, lack of control, negative halo effect, growth challenges, restriction on sale, and poor execution. Access to funding is an advantage.

questions.text: In the Philippines, where is a sole proprietorship's business name reserved and registered?
questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship's name is registered in the DTI Business Name Registration System (BNRS). Partnerships and corporations register their names with the SEC.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as requirements for registering a sole proprietorship?
options: Draft of the articles of partnership
Copy of a government-issued ID as proof of citizenship
Signed copy of the undertaking from the DTI BNRS
questions.explanation: The requirements are the business name, the applicant's TIN, a copy of a government-issued ID, a signed undertaking from the DTI BNRS, and payment for the application. Articles of partnership are for partnerships.

questions.text: In the sole proprietorship registration process, what comes right after getting the certificate from DTI?
options: Securing business registration from the local government (Barangay Certificate, Mayor's Permit & Licenses)
questions.explanation: After the DTI certificate, the owner secures business registration from the local government of the chosen location, then registers with the BIR, and, if there are employees, with SSS, PhilHealth and HDMF.

questions.text: If a business has employees, which of the following must it also register with, according to the module?
questions.explanation: Businesses with employees register with SSS, PhilHealth, and HDMF. The SEC is for registering partnerships and corporations.

questions.text: Match each abbreviation from the business registration process to what it stands for.
allChoices: DTI Business Name Registration System
Bureau of Internal Revenue
Social Security System
Philippine Health Insurance Corporation
Home Development Mutual Fund
questions.explanation: BNRS is the DTI Business Name Registration System, BIR is the Bureau of Internal Revenue, SSS is the Social Security System, PhilHealth is the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation, and HDMF is the Home Development Mutual Fund.

questions.text: Which SEC form is required for a partnership with foreigner partners?
questions.explanation: SEC form F-105 is for foreigner partners. F-100 is the form listed for corporations.

questions.text: According to the module, how many shareholders must a corporation have?
questions.explanation: The corporation requirements state that it "must have at least 5-15 shareholders."

questions.text: What is the minimum paid-up capital for a Filipino corporation, according to the module?
questions.explanation: A Filipino corporation needs at least Php 100,000 in paid-up capital. For foreign-owned corporations the minimum is expected to be higher, depending on the type of corporation.

questions.text: Which SEC form is listed for a corporation with more than 40% (foreign ownership)?
questions.explanation: The module lists SEC form F-100 for a corporation with more than 40%. F-105 is the form for foreigner partners in a partnership.

questions.text: Which of the following are documents a corporation submits to the SEC?
questions.explanation: The SEC submission includes the Cover Sheet, Name Verification Slip, Articles of Incorporation, Treasurer's Affidavit, By-Laws, and an undertaking to change name. The Mayor's Permit is secured later from the local government.

questions.text: Under the Magna Carta for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, which total asset value defines a SMALL enterprise?
questions.explanation: The Magna Carta defines MSMEs by asset size: micro is up to P3,000,000, small is P3,000,001 to P15,000,000, and medium is P15,000,001 to P100,000,000.

questions.text: Match each statistic to what it describes about MSMEs (Philippine Statistics Authority, 2015).
allChoices: Share of total establishments that are MSMEs
Share of the total labor force employed by MSMEs
MSMEs' contribution to total value added
Share of all exporters that are MSMEs

pairs.match: Share of total establishments that are MSMEs
Share of the total labor force employed by MSMEs
MSMEs' contribution to total value added
Share of all exporters that are MSMEs

questions.explanation: MSMEs account for 99.5% of establishments, employ 61.6% of the labor force, contribute 36.7% of total value added, and make up 59% of all exporters.

questions.text: In the 2015 distribution of establishments by enterprise size, what percentage of establishments are MICRO enterprises?
questions.explanation: Micro enterprises are 806,609 of 900,914 establishments (89.53%). Small enterprises are 9.59%, medium 0.43%, and large 0.45%. The 29.43% figure is micro enterprises' share of total employment, not of establishments.

questions.text: By total employment, which enterprise size has the LARGEST share?
questions.explanation: Large enterprises have 2,981,819 of the 7,766,689 total employed (38.39%), even though they are only 0.45% of establishments.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as NON-FINANCIAL barriers to MSME growth and development?
options: Lack of awareness of national and international standards
questions.explanation: Lack of access to finance is the one financial barrier. The non-financial barriers include poor business environment and high cost of doing business, lack of access to market, lack of awareness of standards, low productivity and efficiency, and dealing with climate change and other risks.

questions.text: Match each Republic Act to its title.
allChoices: Magna Carta for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
Barangay Micro Business Enterprises (BMBEs) Act
Go Negosyo Act

pairs.match: Magna Carta for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

questions.explanation: R.A. 6977 is the Magna Carta for MSMEs, R.A. 9178 is the BMBEs Act, and R.A. 10644 is the Go Negosyo Act.

questions.text: Which of the following are major provisions of R.A. 6977 (Magna Carta for MSMEs)?
options: Creation of the Small Business Guarantee and Finance Corporation (SB Corporation)
Mandatory allocation of credit resources for MSME lending
questions.explanation: R.A. 6977 created the MSMED Council and the SB Corporation and required mandatory allocation of credit resources for MSME lending. Establishing Negosyo Centers comes from the Go Negosyo Act (R.A. 10644).

questions.text: Which of the following incentives are given to Barangay Micro Business Enterprises (BMBEs) under R.A. 9178?
options: Exemption from the coverage of the Minimum Wage Law
questions.explanation: BMBEs get exemption from income tax, exemption from the Minimum Wage Law, a special credit window, and technology transfer, production and management training, and marketing assistance.

questions.text: Which of the following are services offered through Negosyo Centers to promote ease of doing business for MSMEs?
questions.explanation: The four services shown are business registration assistance, business advisory services, business information and advocacy, and monitoring and evaluation. Loan collection is not one of them.

questions.text: Under BSP Circular No. 625 (Series of 2008), banks must set aside what share of their total loan portfolio for MSME credit?
options: At least 8% for micro and small enterprises and at least 2% for medium enterprises
At least 2% for micro and small enterprises and at least 8% for medium enterprises
At least 10% for micro enterprises and at least 5% for small enterprises
questions.explanation: The circular requires at least 8% for micro and small enterprises and at least 2% for medium enterprises, for ten years from the effectivity of R.A. 9501.

questions.text: Which program is described as the government's flagship program for the MSME sector, aimed at creating an MSME-friendly lending environment?
options: ASENSO (Access of Small Enterprises to Sound Lending Opportunities)
questions.explanation: ASENSO is the flagship program in which government financial institutions extend loans to MSMEs on manageable terms. It reported P207.448B released (2011-2015), 249,606 MSME borrowers, and 2.618M jobs.

questions.text: Which agency administers the Pondo sa Pagbabago at Pag-asenso (P3) Program?
options: Small Business Corporation, an attached agency of the DTI
questions.explanation: The Small Business Corporation, an attached agency of the DTI, administers P3. Its primary beneficiaries are microenterprises and entrepreneurs without easy access to credit, or who pay very high interest.

questions.text: Match each MSME development initiative to its description.
allChoices: Flagship lending program with GFIs extending loans on manageable terms
Alternative, easy-to-access financing for microenterprises
Continuous learning program to enhance MSME competitiveness
Coaching and mentoring by business owners and practitioners, held in Negosyo Centers
Enhancing industry competitiveness to develop exports, generate investments and create jobs
Provides machinery, equipment, tools and systems under a shared system

pairs.match: Flagship lending program with GFIs extending loans on manageable terms
Continuous learning program to enhance MSME competitiveness
Coaching and mentoring by business owners and practitioners, held in Negosyo Centers
Enhancing industry competitiveness to develop exports, generate investments and create jobs
Provides machinery, equipment, tools and systems under a shared system

questions.explanation: ASENSO is the lending flagship, P3 is alternative financing for microenterprises, SME Roving Academy is a continuous learning program, Mentor ME provides coaching and mentoring in Negosyo Centers, Industry Clustering enhances industry competitiveness and exports, and SSF provides shared machinery, equipment and skills.

questions.text: Which of the following are part of the DTI's 7Ms for MSME Development?
questions.explanation: The 7Ms are Mindset, Money, Mentoring, Machines, Mastery, Business Models, and Markets. Marketing and Manpower are not among them.

questions.text: The SME Development Plan 2017-2022 envisions an MSME sector "performing as one of the most effective drivers of ___ Philippine economic growth."
questions.explanation: The vision ends: "...one of the most effective drivers of inclusive Philippine economic growth."

questions.text: In the MSME Development Framework (2017-2022), match each theme to the focus area it falls under.
allChoices: Business Environment
Business Capacity
Business Opportunities
questions.explanation: Business Environment covers Business Climate and Access to Finance. Business Capacity covers Human Capital Development and Technology and Innovation. Business Opportunities covers Access to Market.
